sentences.text: The 37-year-old, known to his supporters as Danny Tommo, was arrested after the livestreamed video on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Daniel Thomas pleads not guilty after dinghy slashed

sentences.text: Thomas, who appeared at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in Hampshire via videolink, is also charged with failing to disclose the PIN to his phone.
sentences.article_title: Daniel Thomas pleads not guilty after dinghy slashed

sentences.text: He pleaded not guilty to both charges and was remanded in custody until his next court appearance at Portsmouth Crown Court on 29 September.

sentences.text: Prosecutor Kevin Lucie, outlining the facts of the criminal damage charge, told the court that Thomas slashed an adrift boat with a knife and said: "You are on English territory.

sentences.text: This is not France any more." Deputy Chief Magistrate Tan Ikram said the case could have been heard in the magistrates' court but Mr Thomas elected to be tried at crown court.

sentences.text: Cyber-criminals who hacked the FBI say they have extremely sensitive medical data for thousands of its special agents.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: BBC News has seen samples of the stolen "fitness-for-work" medical examinations, which contain information such as blood and urine test results, and doctors' notes mentioning conditions such as a "shellfish and banana allergy".
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: The records include agents' full names and addresses, as well as references to medical concerns including 'blood in the urine' and 'high cholesterol'.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: Experts say the hack - which the FBI is investigating - could leave agents vulnerable to scams, blackmail and targeted attacks, as well as help criminals impersonate law enforcement officers.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: "The list maps thousands of agents against their medical and fitness records," said Etay Maor, vice-president of threat intelligence at Cato Networks.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: "Passwords can be reset if stolen, but medical records cannot, so once this data is out, it stays compromised for good.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: That permanence, applied across an entire workforce, is what makes this leak so serious." The FBI has not responded to requests for comment.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: However, on Wednesday it acknowledged the breach and said it was "aggressively investigating" how it happened.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: The cyber-criminal group ShinyHunters claims it breached FBI systems on Monday, and later posted details of the attack on its darknet site.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: The group also shared samples of the alleged stolen data with reporters, along with an extortion demand.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: Unusually, the hackers are not demanding money.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: Instead, they are seeking a retraction of an FBI advisory published in May, which they claim "offended" them.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: The samples shared with journalists appear genuine and include names, addresses, phone numbers, badge numbers, job titles and information about spouses.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: The records appear to relate to thousands of agents, including senior officials such as deputy directors.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: Reporting by 404 Media suggests details of a previously little-known FBI hacking unit may also have been exposed , external .
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: It was initially thought the breach affected the FBI's 38,000 current employees, but the hackers now claim the number could be far higher.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: The group says it underestimated the scale of the data theft and now claims to hold sensitive information on around 60,000 current and former FBI staff.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: Jamie Akhtar, chief executive and co-founder of CyberSmart, said the hackers' claims should be treated with caution but that the breach appeared to be extremely concerning.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: "Such data could be used for highly convincing phishing, impersonation, identity fraud, blackmail or even operations targeting law-enforcement personnel, making the potential implications particularly serious," he said.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: The hackers, who communicate with reporters in English via the messaging service, Telegram, say they will publish the full dataset in five days unless the FBI meets their demands.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: ShinyHunters is an international hacking collective that has been active since 2019 and has been linked to a number of high-profile cyber-attacks, including incidents affecting Rockstar Games and the education platform Canvas .
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: In a statement posted on X, the FBI said it was still trying to determine whether the hackers had breached its systems directly or compromised a third-party provider.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: "We are actively and aggressively investigating this matter and working closely with those third-party providers that support FBIJobs.gov to mitigate any and all risk," the statement said.
sentences.article_title: Special agents' blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack

sentences.text: Jeffrey Donaldson, pictured in May during his trial, was convicted of 18 counts of sex abuse The victims of child sex offender Jeffrey Donaldson have described the impact the abuse had on them.
sentences.article_title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse

sentences.text: Donaldson was convicted in June of 18 counts of sex abuse including one of rape , which he committed against two women when they were children.
sentences.article_title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse

sentences.text: The former Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader appeared at Newry Crown Court for a hearing prior to his sentencing in October.
sentences.article_title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse

sentences.text: He is seeking to appeal his convictions.
sentences.article_title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse

sentences.text: The prosecution barrister told the court that one of the women said her childhood had been stolen, while the second said the abuse affected her every day.
sentences.article_title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse

sentences.text: In her submission to the pre-sentencing hearing, Rosemary Walsh KC outlined what she described as the "salient facts" that were heard during the course of the trial.
sentences.article_title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse

sentences.text: She also described the impact the offending had on both victims, whom were described during the trial as Complainants A and B.
sentences.article_title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse

sentences.text: She said both complainants often wondered what life would have been like if they hadn't experienced the abuse.
sentences.article_title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse

sentences.text: In her victim impact statement, Complainant A described the "profound impact" the abuse had on her.
sentences.article_title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse

sentences.text: Walsh said the complainant believed her childhood had been "stolen" and that she felt an "enormous amount of anger that is always simmering away under the surface".
sentences.article_title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse

sentences.text: Walsh said the abuse Complainant B had suffered affected her "every day and every relationship", and that she had to fight on a daily basis the wish that she would die.
sentences.article_title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse

sentences.text: Donaldson's defence barrister Keiron Vaughan KC told the court that the 63-year-old was "of previous good character" and that there had been no offending of this type over the last 18 years.
sentences.article_title: Jeffrey Donaldson victim describes 'profound impact' of child sex abuse

sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: "In the UK you have to ask for the account number and sort code, and not everyone has that on hand," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'We're all broke': Would you chase a friend for £5?

sentences.text: President Xi Jinping's summits with Donald Trump have one clear aim.

sentences.text: China believes the United States is trying to contain its rise as a superpower, and it wants Washington to stay out of its way - particularly when it comes to trade, technology and Taiwan.

sentences.text: On this visit, however, despite Trump rolling out the red carpet for him, the Chinese leader didn't get everything he wanted.
sentences.article_title: Xi got Trump's red carpet welcome - but not everything he wanted

sentences.text: The trade truce that saw both countries pause a tit-for-tat tariff war and prevent a further escalation, was extended by only a few months - from November to January.

sentences.text: Beijing had hoped for at least a year as Xi looks to ride out the remainder of Trump's presidency.
sentences.article_title: Xi got Trump's red carpet welcome - but not everything he wanted

sentences.text: When Antonia Duffin, 34, started going to the gym, she wanted to lose weight and tone up.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: It became such a big part of her life that she decided to become a personal trainer alongside her day job in operations for a supermarket chain - and now runs her own women's gym in Manchester.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: "Some of my clients want to feel stronger, some want to get in shape for a baby and some are struggling with other conditions like endometriosis and want to feel better," she says.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Hybrid training, like Hyrox, which is sociable and competitive, seems to have taken over from running on a treadmill or general cardio on a bike, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Antonia also notes an appetite for more strength training workouts among younger clients, adding: "I think people are now realising the importance of it - we're preventing osteoporosis and things like that." Do numbers bear that out?
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: And how are workouts across the UK changing?
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: This video can not be played Why more young people are switching from cardio to weights According to Sport England, more young adults are going to the gym, using exercise machines and weights to keep fit compared to nine years ago.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: "Gyms offer broader types of exercise, like resistance training, which can improve body composition and shape more quickly than aerobic exercise training," explains exercise expert Dr Andrew Scott, from the University of Portsmouth.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: He says social media is having an impact too.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: "Lots of people are largely learning from influencers, suggesting 'I can do it, this is what I did and so can you'." Student Will Seward, 19, started going to the gym when he was at secondary school because he wanted to "get stronger and build up his physique".
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: His workouts - usually three a week - have changed over time, from using running machines and exercise bikes initially to more explosive training using weights, to help build athleticism.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: "It's had a real impact on my day to day life," he says, "improving my mood and making me feel generally healthier." Barbells, kettlebells, dumbbells and cable machines are all part of the strength training Antonia offers in her gym space, located in a shipping container.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Recent research suggests doing the recommended two hours of strength training each week may offer many of the same benefits as regular aerobic exercise, such as lowering the risk of dying from heart disease or stroke while also protecting the brain and boosting self-esteem.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: These benefits are not the only appeal of exercise though.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Many say they feel a sense of connection when exercising with other people.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Dr Hussain Al-Zubaidi, a GP, personal trainer and triathlete, says there is now "an enormous ecosystem" for those who are already active, featuring gyms, running clubs, fitness apps, social media and wearable tech.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: How different age groups meet overall exercise targets varies.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Among nearly 2 million participants in Our Future Health - a health and lifestyle questionnaire - younger age groups were more likely to do shorter bursts of vigorous activity every week like fitness classes, aerobics or football.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: While running has fallen in popularity overall, it is still the most common form of exercise for young men and women - and in the top two activities for adults overall.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: And organised, social running is thriving, with children, 20-somethings and over 50s accounting for a growing share of participants in parkruns, which are free to everyone and have over 1,400 events taking place across the UK every weekend.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Prof Esther van Sluijs, professor of behavioural epidemiology from Loughborough University, says community exercise offers social connection.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: When working from home is so common, particularly for young people, "easy access to community clubs close to home is very important", she adds.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: So how much is keeping active costing exercise goers, at a time when budgeting is tight?
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: More than a quarter of 16-34 year olds say paying for gym membership and keeping fit is a top spending priority, over holidays and eating out, data from UK Active shows - up from a fifth in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: A 2026 survey by the Gym Group found a third of Gen Z spent £26-50 per month on health and fitness, with a quarter spending more than £50.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Events manager Cordelia Sheridan, 27, who exercises four to five times a week at her gym in Battersea, says she treats her £45 gym membership "like an essential utility bill".
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: "If you go to the pub and you're with a group of mates, you can buy a few pints and easily spend that on a night out," she says.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Living just five minutes walk from her gym makes it easy to get there for 6.30am and exercise before work.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Cordelia has changed her gym routine to incorporate more strength training At the gym, she spends 10 minutes on a stair-climbing machine then 35 minutes using weights and machines to strengthen the thighs, hips and lower back.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Before, her routine was all about cardio - but she didn't feel she was getting better or stronger.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Now, she says, it's really nice being able to hit targets and lift heavier weights.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: "I want to go into my 30s being strong." "And it's also weirdly more sociable," she says.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: Persuading people to exercise is about making it the easy, social and enjoyable thing to do, even if it costs, says Dr Al-Zubaidi.
sentences.article_title: Treadmills to deadlifts: Why Gen Z are swapping cardio for strength training

sentences.text: "I think that's why activities like the gym, running clubs and padel have been successful - not because they prevent disease but because they are fun and sociable." Wellness habits you can start now - at no (or little) cost £170 a bag?

sentences.text: US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping exchanged warm words at a lavish White House state dinner but gave little indication of progress on pressing issues.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: Xi stressed that they should ensure AI remain "under human control" and act "as responsible major countries", while Trump toasted a future of "harmony, peace and success" for both nations.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: But tensions remain despite the diplomatic niceties, including over Taiwan - with Xi urging Trump earlier in the day to take the "correct position" on the self-governing island which Beijing claims, amid a weapons package paused by Trump.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: Billionaire business leaders and US tech CEOs joined the leaders at the extravagant dinner late on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: Their arrival was marked by protesters shouting from just outside the White House gates, some of whom were arrested.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: Trump lavished praise on Xi during his first visit to the US in over a decade, telling those attending the dinner that while the two countries had "different systems", they had "never gotten along better".
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: Xi meanwhile welcomed the "historic juncture" in US-China relations - and said both leaders' ambitions could "surely be mutually reinforcing".
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: "China and the United States must act as responsible major countries to meet the expectations of our peoples, keep pace with the trend of our times, and explore a new approach for major countries to get along with each other," he said.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: While Xi said he and Trump had shared "in-depth exchanges and reached common understanding on many issues", little mention was made of the crucial matters which divide the leaders of the world's two most powerful countries.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: China believes the US is trying to contain its rise as a superpower, and it wants Washington to stay out of its way - particularly when it comes to trade, technology and Taiwan.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: Trump has meanwhile been expected to aim for deals around trade and tariffs during the visit – like lowering Chinese tariffs on American goods, increasing imports of Chinese rare earth minerals, and increasing exports of US agricultural products.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: Xi thanked his hosts for receiving him and his wife with "meticulous care and consideration" Trump has been blunt about his ambitions for artificial intelligence (AI) - and clear that he considers China to be the US's main rival for its development.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: But beyond Xi's reference to AI remaining under "human control", little indication was given of what progress the two leaders may have made on the issue during their talks.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: The dinner also came just hours after Chinese state media reported Xi had, behind closed doors, advised Washington to handle "with prudence" its approach to Taiwan.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: Washington is yet to comment publicly on the remarks.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: The US is legally bound to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself, but Trump delayed approving a $14bn (£11bn) arms package for it after Xi in May warned that mishandling the issue could cause the two countries to "collide or even enter into conflict".
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: At the time, Trump called it a "very good negotiating chip" with Beijing.
sentences.article_title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words but little progress on key issues

sentences.text: Dan Robathan spent years climbing the football ladder as an assistant referee It was May 2025 and life was good for Premier League and Fifa assistant referee Dan Robathan.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: In fact, he was flying high.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: Years of climbing the football ladder had paid off and he was running the line at the FA Cup final between Crystal Palace and Manchester City.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: But just months after this career highlight, symptoms Dan thought were sciatic nerve pain and wear and tear were revealed to be benign tumours in his spine, which needed to be operated on immediately.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "I saw a neurosurgeon who told me I had two tumours, initially I thought it was one, but it was two," Dan tells BBC Newsbeat.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "It was compressing nerves, there was a chance it could affect a motor nerve which means it could affect function in my leg.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "I needed to go home, lay down and not move.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: I did that for 15 days, my life turned upside down overnight." BBC Newsbeat met Dan at a football pitch in Norwich, close to where he lives, where he revealed the struggles he has had in trying to regain his fitness and mobility.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: Dan Robathan (centre) worked his way up to top flight football Dan picked up his first flag at 10 years old, working his way up from grassroots football to the lines at more than 200 Premier League clashes and World Cup qualifiers.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: Speaking at the time of the FA Cup final, Dan said it was "a privilege to stand there on behalf of over 37,000 referees across the country".
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: The chances of becoming an elite level referee are low.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: The FA describes Fifa match officials , external as the "pinnacle of the officiating ladder".
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: Photos of Dan over the last few years show him doing everything from embracing then Liverpool manager Arne Slot to explaining a decision to Emiliano Martinez, and officiating games without fans due to the Covid pandemic.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: And in his social media posts, Dan gives a glimpse of everything you would expect from an official at elite level - from the roar of fans to sprinting to be in the right place during split second decisions.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: To the outside world, all looked well.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "I started having quite bad problems with sexual dysfunction or bladder issues where I'd have to sit down to urinate and I couldn't stand up," he explains.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "It got to a point in September [2025] where something's not right at all." A neurosurgeon confirmed to Dan he had two tumours in his spine – and his life ground to a halt.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "It was fear, anxiety, not knowing how long it will take me to get back.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "What would my life look like?
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: Will I walk again?" Surgeons removed one tumour and left one alone, which was deemed safe.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: Dan says he needs time to "grieve" his career - but has hope for the future The tumours were non-cancerous, but have caused significant damage to Dan, who describes his post-operation recovery as "brutal".
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: Yet there was "no doubt" in his mind that he would return.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: But by Christmas 2025, Dan was still feeling fatigued and struggling to lift his heel, walk, or feel his calf.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "The surgeon said I had under a 10% chance of ever getting back on the field but even then I was like I don't care I will prove everyone wrong," Dan recalls.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: Yet despite fighting "like mad", he was unable to regain his fitness levels.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: This week, Dan was forced to medically retire, saying in effect "the decision was made for me".
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: Dan says he wants to help other men speak up about health problems The 38-year-old says he still has days where he struggles to walk, or where his back feels "on fire".
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "My body just can't do what I want it to do," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: Dan underwent testing to confirm his tumours weren't linked to genetics, which was reassuring, but still leaves him facing the unknown.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "It's a loss of identity.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: I've been 'Dan the ref' since I was 10 years old.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "It's 28 years of being who I am, it's my personality.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "When you have the recognition that that sort of life is over, psychologically it is really tough." Dan is now working with a psychologist to decide the path forward.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "I feel like a 16-year-old who's just left school and trying to work out what I want to do with my life," he jokes.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "I have a few options, staying in football.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "[But] I don't know if I will be able to with the mental health problems I've had.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "Can I stay involved in a sport that I loved but can't do myself?" One thing he is certain of, is going into the future with his family.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "I want to put my son, fiancée, my stepchildren first.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: I want to try and advocate for men's mental health, for men speaking about health issues.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: "If I can help one or two men in the process, I've done my job." And Dan accepts that if he gets back into football it would need to be for the right reasons.
sentences.article_title: 'I was living out my dream career in football – tumours mean I need to leave'

sentences.text: The test means patients can be diagnosed within hours rather than weeks, like Steve Palmer whose case the BBC followed A rapid new test for brain tumours that the NHS has started using can slash the time it takes for an accurate diagnosis from up to eight weeks to two hours.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: The test, which is used by doctors to diagnose which type of tumour a patient has, should mean patients can start treatment including radiotherapy and chemotherapy sooner, and are spared weeks of uncertainty.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: Steve Palmer, 55, from Nottingham, is among those to benefit from the new technology - and it meant surgeons were able to get his result while they were still operating to remove his tumour.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: "Getting that quick diagnosis removed weeks of anxiety," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: NHS England said that the genomic test, which works by quickly analysing the genetic code of a sample of the tumour, will be piloted in specialist centres around England.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: There are around 150 different types of brain tumour ranging from slow-growing to aggressive cancers, each of which can respond differently to treatment.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: Steve was diagnosed with a brain tumour after he collapsed at the gym, and the test revealed it to be a grade 4 glioblastoma.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: "It wasn't the result I wanted to hear but it means I can get on with the next phase of treatment and recovery, and get on with fighting whatever it is I've got to fight," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: Here it is done while we are still operating." Diagnosing the type of tumour while the patient is still on the operating table could impact how surgeons operate.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: Smith explained: "For some tumour types, which are curable, surgery needs to be as radical as possible to remove every last bit of tumour that we can find.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: The samples are prepared for loading into a shoebox-sized sequencing machine made by Oxford Nanopore, which uses specialist software developed at the University of Nottingham, in partnership with hospital clinicians.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: The molecules of DNA pass through a nanopore - a tiny hole - which reveals the tumour's unique genomic fingerprint.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: In Steve's case, after the nanopore machine was running for 20 minutes, the neuropathology team called the theatre to tell them that the tumour was likely to be a glioblastoma.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: Dr Simon Paine, consultant neuropathologist at Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust, explained that the genomic test was transformative in comparison to what he could determine by looking at tumour cells down a microscope.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: "I'm crystal ball gazing and can do it reasonably well on a good day, but nowhere near with the clarity of the nanopore, which gives a comprehensive molecular classification," he said.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: More than 12,000 people in the UK are diagnosed with a primary brain tumour each year.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: It is the biggest cancer killer of children and adults under 40.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: Prof Frankie Swords, NHS medical director, said: "For people with suspected brain tumours, getting the right diagnosis quickly can feel like a race against time, while waiting weeks for answers can be agonising for them and their families.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: "This remarkable rapid test has the potential to completely transform how we diagnose brain tumours, with results reaching patients in a matter of days rather than weeks.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: It will later be extended to sites in Bristol, Oxford, Leeds and Manchester.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: The pilot builds on an earlier project already under way in Nottingham and Birmingham.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: "Rapid genomic testing could dramatically shorten the wait for answers for brain tumour patients and, in some cases, give surgeons vital information before an operation is even over.
sentences.article_title: Brain tumour diagnosis cut from weeks to hours with rapid new test

sentences.text: Transport committee member Collette Stevenson says she suffered a momentary lapse of concentration during a meeting earlier this month An MSP who faced ridicule over a blunder at a Holyrood committee has said she suffered a "momentary lapse"  brought on by lack of sleep and a chest infection.
sentences.article_title: Ridiculed MSP says chest infection and lack of sleep led to committee blunder

sentences.text: Collette Stevenson, who has represented East Kilbride for the SNP since 2021 and is a member of the transport committee,  was criticised after asking if Transport Scotland was a registered charity.
sentences.article_title: Ridiculed MSP says chest infection and lack of sleep led to committee blunder

sentences.text: Transport Scotland director Graeme Cook then explained to her that it was a national agency which was part of the Scottish government.
sentences.article_title: Ridiculed MSP says chest infection and lack of sleep led to committee blunder

sentences.text: Posting on Facebook, Stevenson said her illness had affected her concentration, and said she had been subjected to "misogynistic bullying" following the incident.
sentences.article_title: Ridiculed MSP says chest infection and lack of sleep led to committee blunder

sentences.text: The 57-year-old added that she later took a week off work, on medical advice, to recuperate.
sentences.article_title: Ridiculed MSP says chest infection and lack of sleep led to committee blunder

sentences.text: She posted: "During a recent committee evidence session, I experienced a momentary lapse in my questioning regarding the status of Transport Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Ridiculed MSP says chest infection and lack of sleep led to committee blunder

sentences.text: "I was in the early stages of a severe chest infection, which affected my sleep and, in turn, my concentration.
sentences.article_title: Ridiculed MSP says chest infection and lack of sleep led to committee blunder

sentences.text: She has previously asked questions during committee meetings about the Clyde Metro development - a key recommendation from Transport Scotland's strategic transport review - and worked with the body on the East Kilbride rail enhancement and electrification project.
sentences.article_title: Ridiculed MSP says chest infection and lack of sleep led to committee blunder

sentences.text: But earlier this month, after about two hours of evidence on Scotland's rail services, Stevenson asked: "I take it Transport Scotland is a registered charity?" "Transport Scotland is a non-departmental government body," Graeme Cook, director of rail delivery for Transport Scotland, responded.
sentences.article_title: Ridiculed MSP says chest infection and lack of sleep led to committee blunder

sentences.text: "Transport Scotland is an agency so all of the Transport Scotland staff are already part of the civil service.
sentences.article_title: Ridiculed MSP says chest infection and lack of sleep led to committee blunder

sentences.text: "Transport Scotland is the same legal entity as the Scottish government." Stevenson said that since her mistake she had been ridiculed and bullied online.
sentences.article_title: Ridiculed MSP says chest infection and lack of sleep led to committee blunder

sentences.text: After the incident, SNP minister Stephen Gethins stood up for Stevenson's character, describing her as "a really good colleague and fantastic local advocate".

sentences.text: Now Nasa is working around that problem using the X-59's elongated snout to flatten supersonic booms into tolerable bumps in the background.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: On top of its bizarre appearance the X-59 boasts a remarkable lineage.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It's the latest in a series of experimental Nasa aircraft dating back to 1947 and the first plane to break the sound barrier, the Bell X-1.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Peter Coen, a 43-year Nasa veteran who manages the programme, explains the thinking behind 80 years of X-planes.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "Our approach is to pick small goals we aim to prove with flight data and we construct an airframe for that one task." The X-plane philosophy is to "minimise goals, the more goals you have the more expensive it gets." For the X-59 it's about suppressing sonic booms on a budget and nothing else.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In the case of the X-1, flown through the sound barrier in 1947 by the legendary test pilot Chuck Yeager, Nasa knew a .50 calibre bullet travelled faster than the speed of sound.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: So the stumpy little aircraft was shaped like a bullet with wings added.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A mere 20 years later the X-15 rocket plane, a cylinder with tiny wings dropped from a B-52 bomber, flew to 6.7 times the speed of sound (4,520 mph) and the edge of space, paving the way for heat-resistant materials vital to the Space Shuttle.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In 1947 the Bell X-1 was the first plane to break the sound barrier Nasa is flying the X-59 in conjunction with community surveys to assess what people think when a supersonic boom is bent by the planes stretched nose and hushed up.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "We want to figure out what level of boom is acceptable to people on a regular basis," says Coen, who reckons his machine will sound "like a car door being closed across the street" when it flies past Mach 1, around 660mph at airline cruising altitude.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: With its cockpit and ejector seat taken from a T-38 training jet, its landing gear from an F-16 fighter and engine courtesy of the F-18 this jigsaw of an aircraft was assembled by Lockheed Martin for Nasa.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A camera feeding a screen in front of the pilot relies on instantaneous computer processing to get round the lack of forward vision.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It first flew in 2025 and is now breaking the sound barrier over chosen US towns.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: But is there still a place for X-plane projects in a world where relatively cheap drones are being rapidly developed - not least in Ukraine's war against Russia .
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Even Nasa considered an uncrewed X-59.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: But drones are not always a cheaper option.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Plus the X-59 had to be big enough to resemble an airliner punching through the sound barrier, which in turn allowed space for a cockpit.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Small was beautiful for the tiny X-48 with its 20ft wingspan as this kept the programme within budget.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "It's likely that future X-planes will be uncrewed," says Coen, before adding the vital caveats "unless the technology we're researching relates to piloting or if crewing it is more cost-effective".
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: The X-48 was a scaled-down plane to test a blended wing and fuselage Guy Gratton, professor of Aircraft Test and Evaluation at Cranfield University, gets frustrated at the suggestion crewed test planes have had their day.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "There's a belief in certain quarters that drones can do everything.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: In Ukraine they've done amazing things with drones, but if you want to carry people you can't take short-cuts." Gratton has tested light aircraft and stresses the importance of a human in the loop.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "You lose a huge amount without pilots, you miss lessons a pilot would identify, plus it can take four times as many people on the ground to test a drone." Staff monitoring signals from a drone are an indirect cost that keeps some piloted X-planes relatively affordable.

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "They all research some facet of flight, and demonstrate the design is working correctly.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: A lot of people say they can do something, but you only know it works when the design has been tested and certified." Forty years on from Yeo's EAP flights a new UK technology demonstrator is taking shape.

sentences.text: It is, says Tony Godbold who runs the project for BAE Systems, "the X-plane of our generation".

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: Wetherspoon staff have been turning away up to 20 tourists on a daily basis as scammers use the address as a fake Booking.com holiday apartment, Which? has found A theatre-goer fell victim to a "sophisticated phishing attack" after booking a "luxury" London apartment, only to discover the address was a Wetherspoon pub.
sentences.article_title: Scam hotel booking sent family to Wetherspoon pub

sentences.text: Paul Dawson, from Loughborough in Leicestershire, paid £73 for a one-night stay for his family via Booking.com at The London Crown apartments to watch the musical Hamilton in the West End.
sentences.article_title: Scam hotel booking sent family to Wetherspoon pub

sentences.text: Days later, he said, he discovered the address shown in the listing was actually The Liberty Bounds pub, a Wetherspoon near Tower Bridge.
sentences.article_title: Scam hotel booking sent family to Wetherspoon pub

sentences.text: Consumer protection organisation Which? said Wetherspoon staff had been turning away up to 20 tourists a day after scammers used the pub's address as a listing for a "block of luxury apartments".
sentences.article_title: Scam hotel booking sent family to Wetherspoon pub

sentences.text: Which? said it was also made aware of a property listed as "Apartments near Big Ben", with the address given as Portcullis House, part of the House of Commons estate, where hundreds of MPs work.
sentences.article_title: Scam hotel booking sent family to Wetherspoon pub

sentences.text: Booking.com told Which? that in both cases, listings for legitimate properties had been targeted by a "sophisticated phishing attack, allowing criminals to hijack the listings".
sentences.article_title: Scam hotel booking sent family to Wetherspoon pub

sentences.text: Wetherspoon said it had informed Booking.com about this scam "as soon as it came to their attention".
sentences.article_title: Scam hotel booking sent family to Wetherspoon pub

sentences.text: Paul Dawson said he had to find alternative accommodation for his family Dawson, 55, made his booking in August.
sentences.article_title: Scam hotel booking sent family to Wetherspoon pub

sentences.article_title: Scam hotel booking sent family to Wetherspoon pub

sentences.text: Dawson told Which? he contacted Booking.com with his suspicions, but said the platform told him that he would need to visit the "fake apartment" and wait until after 7pm before it would relocate him.

sentences.article_title: Scam hotel booking sent family to Wetherspoon pub

sentences.article_title: Scam hotel booking sent family to Wetherspoon pub

sentences.text: The Liberty Bounds is in Trinity Square, Tower Hill, and near the Tower of London The listing for the London Crown apartments had 250 negative reviews from August and September along with a handful of, likely fake, positive reviews, Which? said.

sentences.text: Reports of violent incidents and harassment on rail services "rose substantially" last year, figures from the rail regulator show.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: Reported assaults, including physical and verbal, were up 36% in the year to March 2026 compared with the previous year, according to the Office of Rail and Road (ORR).
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: In total 13,464 assaults against passengers and members of the public were recorded on Britain's mainline railway, the highest number recorded since the series began in 2004.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: The ORR said the figures were "concerning" and that it was working with the industry to address the problem.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: According to the figures, harassment increased by 52%  compared with the previous year and common assaults rose by 30%.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: The increase comes against a backdrop of five years of rising reports of incidents and industry campaigns to raise awareness.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: Assaults on the mainline railway are recorded according to their type.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: As a result each incident can lead to reports in more than one category, for example if someone is harassed and then physically assaulted.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: There were also 11,289 reported assaults against members of the workforce on the mainline railway, up 12% compared with the previous year.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: Of those 2,487 were physical assaults, while more than half (6,390 incidents) involved verbal abuse.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: "We're working with industry and our trade union colleagues to address work-related violence and harassment," said Richard Hines, the ORR's chief inspector of railways.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: "This includes understanding where the risks are, putting effective controls in place, encouraging staff to report incidents and providing appropriate support afterwards," he said.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: The statistics include mainline rail services in England, Scotland and Wales, but not Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: The data release also covers the London Underground, trams, metros and other light rail services.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: On the London Underground, recorded assaults increased 20% to 5,534 in the latest year, but reported workforce assaults fell 3% to 3,525.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: Transport for London does not record multiple aspects of each incident.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: Instead it records the most severe aspect reported.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: A spokesperson responding on behalf of Network Rail and the train companies said all operators were working to reduce risk and prevent harm by sharing information, improving reporting processes and deploying body-worn cameras.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: "Keeping passengers and colleagues safe is at the heart of everything we do," the spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: "Violence, abuse and intimidation directed at passengers or staff are completely unacceptable.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: The rail industry works closely with British Transport Police to investigate incidents, support victims and bring offenders to justice." The passenger body, Transport Focus, said the ORR's figures supported research it conducted which found personal security was "one of the highest priorities" for passengers.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: However, only 3% of passengers it surveyed said they were dissatisfied with personal safety at the station.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: Transport Focus acknowledged that some of the increase might reflect better reporting.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: Nevertheless, every incident represented someone negatively affected, it said, adding it would like to see "a much more strategic approach" to tackling the issue.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: The RMT union, representing rail industry workers, said the figures corresponded with the union's own figures indicating two-thirds of its members had experienced violence at work.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: RMT general secretary Eddie Dempsey called for an increase in staffing on public transport, including an end to lone working, to combat the problem.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: "We also clearly need stronger legal protections for public transport workers against assaults at work," he said.
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: He said cuts to British Transport Police funding had been "disastrous" and called for outsourced security and enforcement staff to be brought in-house "as a matter of urgency".
sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.article_title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third

sentences.text: Eight were pedestrians and the others were road vehicle users.

sentences.text: Lidl must stop selling Birkenstock copies, including sandals based on the "Arizona" worn here by actor Jason Mamoa Lidl must stop selling copycat versions of Birkenstock's famous sandals in the Netherlands, a Dutch court has ruled.
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: The discount supermarket chain faces a fine of €5,000 (£4,200) per day if it fails to comply and must also hand over sales data to Birkenstock, according to the ruling.
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: Lidl must also compensate Birkenstock and pay its legal fees, with the amount to be decided in separate court decisions.
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: Birkenstock said the judgement sent a clear message that "copycats must not be allowed to free-ride on [our] creativity and innovation".
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: The BBC has contacted Lidl for comment.
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: The ruling, which can still be appealed against, means Lidl cannot sell its copycat versions of Birkenstock's Arizona, Madrid, Gizeh, Boston, and Florida models across the Netherlands, after the court found the discount grocer infringed on the brand's trademark "footbed design".
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: It is the latest in a string of court decisions on Birkenstock designs.
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: In November 2025, a Dutch court order stopped retailer Scapino from selling similar lookalikes in a judgment which is being appealed against.
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: And in December 2025, Europe's highest court ruled everyday commercial products can hold copyright if they represent creative design choices, a decision which Birkenstock said was relevant to its "iconic" sandals.
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: However, Birkenstock also faced a setback in Germany's highest court in early 2025.
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: The sandals may have been cool enough for Margot Robbie to wear in the Barbie film, but the German judges ruled they were practical products rather than works of art – an outcome Birkenstock called a "missed opportunity" at the time.
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: Following Wednesday's ruling, Birkenstock said it will "continue to defend its rights vigorously and will use all available legal means to combat imitations of its iconic products".
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: "To protect its retail partners and consumers, Birkenstock will continue to take decisive action against copycats seeking to profit from the company's creative ideas and innovations," it added.
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: Birkenstock is far from the only fashion brand locked in battles with mass retailers over design mimicry.
sentences.article_title: Lidl banned from selling copycat Birkenstock sandals, Dutch court rules

sentences.text: Footwear giants like Dr. Martens have repeatedly taken online big-box sellers to court over boot designs, while luxury house Christian Louboutin spent years in global litigation defending its signature red soles against high-street copycats.

sentences.text: Sam Altman of OpenAI has become a key figure in the AI technology development.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: The heads of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Hugging Face have told the UN that the current pace of artificial intelligence (AI) development, and the risks it poses to society, demands international coordination.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: Altman called for common risk evaluation standards, as did Dario Amodei of Anthropic, a main rival of OpenAI, and Clement Delangue of Hugging Face.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: Earlier this month, Amodei wrote an essay welcomed by Altman and others calling an AI development slowdown in response to fears about the technology's threat to humanity.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: However, at the same UN conference, a key technology advisor to US President Donald Trump, rejected the idea any new form of AI regulation.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: Michael Kratsios, a former Scale AI executive, admitted that the speed of AI development is increasing and that there are risks presented by the technology, but told the UN this was not reason enough "to pause development or constrain it with new global governance structures".
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: "International dialogue in this forum and others cannot be allowed to drift toward global governance," Kratsios added.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: Kratsios's comments echoed similar statements made by Trump in recent weeks.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: Trump told the UN on Tuesday he wanted to rebrand it "super intelligence" and has strongly opposed any idea of an AI slowdown because of the US's competitive advantage in the sector.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: "We're leading China on AI... and, frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins ," he said earlier this month.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: Sam Altman of OpenAI and other AI chief executives expressed a different view in their talks to the UN on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: "If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone," said Altman.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: He told the UN that he wanted countries to start working together toward "the collective good in the face of powerful new technology".
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: He called for "national and international" AI standards on measuring the capabilities of an AI tool, assessing related risks, AI safeguards, and the degree to which human oversight over such tools is maintained.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: He also called for "speedy incident reporting, classification, and reporting protocols so the world can learn from failures before they become catastrophes".
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: "We need common standards so countries can compare evidence, verify compliance, and have a shared language and understanding what is happening," Altman added.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: Not all AI workers think the tech could kill everyone AI 'kill switch' may need to be mandatory, Anthropic co-founder tells BBC AI staff 'genuinely frightened' for humanity's future, ex-Anthropic researcher tells BBC Anthropic's Amodei and Hugging Face's Delangue made similar comments in their speeches.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: Amodei said that AI "if managed poorly... could be a risk to humanity as a whole".
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: He added that further development of AI tools calls for "even more stringent standards of safety".
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: "We will slow down as much as necessary in order to make sure that every successive AI technology that we release is actually safe," Amodei added.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: Hugging Face, a platform for AI developers, more recently rose to prominence after it admitted to being hacked by AI agents , or AI bots that operate somewhat autonomously, that came out of OpenAI.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: Hugging Face has since been acquired by AI chipmaker Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: US rejects pleas from OpenAI, Anthropic for global AI standards

sentences.text: The Hugging Face hack has been treated as a 'wake-up call' within the industry for the ways in which AI technology has advanced and could hypothetically act in ways that could harm humanity.

sentences.text: The Torcal will be built on a brand-new production line in Cheshire Bentley has unveiled its first fully electric car after investing £350m to  upgrade its factory in Cheshire.
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: The Torcal SUV will be built on a brand-new production line at the site, which has been the luxury carmaker's headquarters since 1946.
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: Business secretary Jonathan Reynolds said the investment would "support 4,000 high-value local jobs in Crewe".
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: The Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade said the Torcal would strengthen automotive supply chains, as Bentley is supplied by more than 700 businesses including 82 within a 50-mile radius of its base.
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: The announcement comes as the UK motor industry is facing strong headwinds, with JLR recently announcing large-scale job cuts and manufacturers looking for new avenues to grow their businesses .
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: Despite announcements of new electric models to future-proof the industry, there have been calls to slow the switch to a fully EV future .
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: Bentley said the Torcal's 113kWh battery gave it a range of up to 375 miles (600km), adding that it could charge from 10% to 80% in less than 20 minutes using a 400kW charger.
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: The company said the Torcal S model would also be its most powerful car yet with a top speed of 162mph, and the fastest-accelerating from standstill, reaching 60mph in 2.8 seconds.
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: The standard Torcal model can travel at up to 155mph and takes 3.3 seconds to accelerate to 60mph.
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: Materials like leather, wool and aluminium are used in the car's interior Dr Frank-Steffen Walliser, Bentley's chairman and chief executive, called the Torcal "one of the best Bentleys ever" and said it had been designed to combine luxury with electric technology.
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: "The Torcal is a Bentley first and foremost, created by hand by people who care, using the best available materials and technology to blend heritage with cutting-edge innovation," he said.
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: The new Bentley comes in an aluminium finish The new production line is inside one of the Crewe site's original factory buildings dating from 1938.
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: It previously housed the company's machining shop and later its research and development workshop.
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: It has been stripped and fitted with a new floor designed to allow autonomous guided vehicles to move cars through the production process.
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: Reynolds described Bentley's £350m investment as "the third win in just seven days" for Britain's automotive industry following £500m announced by McLaren and £170m from Nissan.
sentences.article_title: Bentley unveils its first fully electric car

sentences.text: The government said it was investing £7.5bn to support a transition to electric vehicles, with plans to phase out new petrol and diesel cars from 2030.
