sentences.text: Lisa Carroll was only 41 was she was diagnosed with the rare form of ovarian cancer A mum-of-three who was diagnosed with a rare cancer has urged other women not to dismiss their symptoms.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: When Lisa Carroll, 47, from Coventry, returned from a family holiday in August 2021, she thought she was suffering from irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), a kidney infection or something minor.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Instead, she was told it was mucinous ovarian cancer (MOC), one of the rarest forms of ovarian cancer in the UK.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "I thought I had possibly a bit of IBS or a kidney problem or something like that.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I was in quite a lot of pain," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Next year, Carroll and her husband are looking forward to celebrating their 20th wedding anniversary After calling NHS 111, Carroll was sent to hospital in Coventry where medics discovered a 12cm cyst on her right ovary.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: She was told it did not appear particularly sinister and was placed on a waiting list for surgery.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "Within a month, a cyst the size of a fist had grown to the point that I could feel it like a football in my stomach.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Pain and discomfort got worse and I felt shattered emotionally and physically", she said.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: By December, scans revealed the tumour had grown to 20cm and was beginning to rupture, so three days later she underwent an emergency procedure to remove the tumour, a fallopian tube, her appendix and surrounding tissue.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Two weeks later, doctors gave her the diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Following surgeries and chemotherapy, Carroll is approaching her five-year anniversary of being cancer free The cancer is exceptionally rare, with only around 200 cases diagnosed annually in the UK, said Ovacome, an ovarian cancer charity.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "Some ovarian cancers are really sneaky, hang around for years and you've got no sign of any symptoms at all", said Carroll, who works as the CEO of Lifespace Trust, a Warwickshire-based charity for young people.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "The fact that mine grew so quickly was what alerted them as early as they did." Yet despite losing her hair and enduring months of treatment, she says the biggest challenge was something she had not been prepared for.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "I got chucked into early menopause and that was the bit I massively struggled with.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I didn't know what was depression and what was menopause." The Ovacome charity is hosting a fundraising walk in Cannon Hill Park, Birmingham on Saturday "I didn't know what was a cancer symptom and what was a menopause symptom.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I couldn't open the washing machine, the dishwasher or the oven.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I couldn't cook anything on the hob because I'd just have this awful hot flush.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: I was incredibly emotional." Today, Carroll is cancer-free and approaching the five-year milestone that will see her formally discharged from oncology care.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "I do not underestimate how fortunate I am that my long-term outlook is a lot brighter than for many," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "That brings with it a kind of survivor's guilt." She has since became involved with Ovacome, which connected her with others facing the same fears.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "They became my safe space," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: "They helped me to connect with other people who understood what I was going through.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: They made an incredibly scary and isolating time feel far more manageable." Now preparing to take part in the charity's annual fundraising walk, Carroll hopes sharing her story will encourage others to trust their instincts and seek help when something feels wrong.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: The fundraising walk takes place at Cannon Hill Park in Birmingham on Saturday.
sentences.article_title: 'A tumour the size of a football saved my life'

sentences.text: Sleep scores, magnesium, white noise machines - what was once the simple act of sleeping has become a minefield.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Trying to optimise sleep in this way is called "sleepmaxxing".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Take it too far, and you could end up with "orthosomnia" - the clinical term for an obsession with achieving perfect sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: While it's not formally recognised as a condition in the UK, doctors tell the BBC they've noticed signs of orthosomnia in their patients, with some bringing their sleep tracker data into appointments convinced, wrongly, that they have a sleep disorder.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: That fixation is actually making people's sleep worse, they warn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: So how and why did sleep become so complicated?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: And if sleepmaxxing isn't the answer, what is the elusive secret to a good night's sleep?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The first commercial fitness tracker to incorporate sleep analysis was the Fitbit Classic in 2009.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Since then, many others - including Garmin, Whoop and Apple - have integrated sleep trackers into wrist-worn devices, as have smart rings such as Oura, Ultrahuman and RingConn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: These devices vary, but in general they all provide users with a report of their night, broken down by sleep stages - time awake, light sleep, deep sleep, and REM (rapid eye movement).
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Many also give users a "sleep score".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: But the concept of a sleep score is "completely made up", according to Dr Alanna Hare, consultant of sleep medicine at the Royal Brompton Hospital in London.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "There's nothing recognised in sleep science that is a 'sleep score'," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That's just been created by manufacturers." This video can not be played How sleep-tracking can make your sleep worse Hare says she's noticed trackers causing anxiety among her patients.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I've noticed more patients coming to me with data from various trackers, with lots of questions about sleep that... is probably contributing to their sleep difficulties," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Even though some have had medical tests with reassuring results, this hasn't allayed their fears, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It's great that there's more focus on sleep as part of wellness," she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "But sleep just does not respond well to attempts to perfect it." One proposed lawsuit against Oura, filed last month in San Francisco, alleges that Oura rings are unable to accurately measure sleep quality and sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that have "a coin flip's chance of being correct".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In response, Oura told the BBC that it "stand[s] behind our science, research and accuracy claims".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "We're committed to clearly communicating what Oura measures, what it estimates, and how members should use that information," the company added.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Studies also show sleep trackers can affect how you function during the day, even if they're not accurate.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In one study , external from the University of Oxford, participants were given sleep trackers which assigned them a sleep score.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The scores were randomised, however, and had no relation to how the participants had actually slept.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The next day participants rated their mood, fatigue levels and alertness, before tests checking their focus and reaction times.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Researchers found that the people told they'd slept badly reported feeling more fatigued, and were less mentally alert - even though the sleep scores were all fake.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: This is something Jess Hill says she noticed in herself after getting a Garmin watch several years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I started to rely on the watch as my Bible for whether I slept well or not," the 32-year-old HR professional from London tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I would think, 'I've had awful sleep so I'm going to really struggle today', even if I actually probably had okay sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I was awake the other week for four hours in the night, and my watch was like 'wow, great sleep!' - I literally was awake from 01:00 until 05:00," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The BBC has approached Garmin for comment.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Jess's sleep scores weren't matching how she actually felt Dr Neil Stanley, sleep expert and author of the book How to Sleep Well, argues that gamifying sleep is creating more disordered sleeping.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "The thing with tracking your sleep is that it gives you a number, and this means you have a target," he tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "So you get into this cycle of worrying about your quality of sleep or the quantity of sleep based on figures." He says he carried out research into actigraphy - wrist-worn sleep trackers - around 40 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Though commercial trackers now are a bit more sophisticated, they work in much the same way - by measuring your movement - and have the same limitations, he says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "If you want to measure sleep, you have to measure the brain," Stanley adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "Unless you're measuring the brain's activities, you're not measuring sleep." Keeping your bedroom cool, dark and quiet - within reason.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That doesn't mean it needs to be pitch black, exactly 16C or totally silent," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It should be coolish, darkish and quietish." Seeing bright light in the morning, which is good for regulating your circadian rhythm - that is, your body's natural clock.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Doing light exercise, and eating a "healthy, Mediterranean-style diet with plenty of plant variability".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Above all, keeping it simple - "anything else, you don't need it".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: England's biggest school leaders' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections, saying they could pose a "risk to life" for school staff.

sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: It said schools should instead be rated using short narrative reports that set out their strengths and areas they could improve.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted, England's schools inspectorate, introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry , who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Sara Kahsai wants all survivors of FGM to seek help and not suffer alone Sara Kahsai grew up in Sudan but moved to Birmingham, England, in 2022 after marrying a bus driver from the city.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But as she settled into married life and her new home, she was coming to terms with a life-changing discovery.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara realised she was a victim-survivor of Female Genital Mutiliation (FGM), a procedure she had endured as a young girl.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was floored by the revelation and, not least, the excruciating pain she was now beginning to fully understand.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "The shock was massive," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It made it difficult with my physical relationship with my husband - but he was very kind and very patient with me." Warning: This story contains descriptions of the practices involved in female genital mutilation Sara turned to the one person she knew must have orchestrated it - her mother - and asked her why.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It was the culture to do it for everybody," she said her mother, still living in Africa, told her.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When I spoke to my mum she was really upset and she apologised to me." FGM involves the partial or total removal of female genitalia for non-medical reasons, and is practiced in some parts of Africa, the Middle East and Asia.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It also happens within some migrant communities in the UK, where it is illegal and treated as child abuse.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It is also against the law to take a girl abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Reasons include social acceptance, religion, misconceptions about hygiene and preserving a girl or woman's virginity.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The Home Office website cites World Health Organisation figures showing three million girls undergo some form , external of the procedure every year in Africa alone.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The mum received help for her FGM after she found out she was pregnant When Sara fell pregnant, she finally told health professionals she had endured FGM as a child.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was immediately referred to the specialist FGM Clinic, run by midwives at Birmingham Women's Hospital.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif deals with around 200 cases each year and says her job is to ensure the wellbeing of women and safeguard unborn children.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "Some types of female circumcision can affect the vaginal delivery," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: They offer deinfibulation - a procedure that can be carried out during pregnancy to separate fused tissue and enable safer births.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: What is FGM, where does it happen and why?
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Victim-survivors of FGM can also experience difficulty with urinating and menstruating, the midwife said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Women are more prone to infections and sepsis, and can suffer from severe and ongoing pain, as well having to deal with psychological trauma, anxiety and depression.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Many patients find it hard to talk to her about what's happened to them, Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It is very difficult, very emotional.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's very difficult for the woman to actually come forward and to come to the clinic, attend the clinic, and have a conversation with me as well," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I explain to them that I'm here to help and I try to explain to them what happened to them when they were a child." She said most women leave the clinic with a better understanding of how they have been affected and how they can take back control of their bodies.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "We talk about every part, what that part is there for and what's been removed and what cause for concern and what effect this will have for the rest of her life," Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Counselling is also offered as well as information on how partners and husbands can support them.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif runs the FGM centre at Birmingham Women's Hospital In 2015, children's charity Barnardo's set up the National FGM Centre to help better protect women and girls.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It works to prevent FGM, raise awareness of it and support those affected.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The centre said schools are legally required to teach pupils about FGM and the law surrounding it as part of relationships and sex education.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But how it is delivered can vary between schools.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's also not mandatory for it to be taught in primary schools and they want to see that change.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "For us, a huge part of tackling FGM is prevention," Rohma Ullah, from the centre, said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Among improvements on the way are new guidelines to help identify girls at risk of being taken abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara wants to urge other women in a similar position to take immediate action.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I have a message to all ladies who've had FGM," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When they come to the UK it is different.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: There's help here - go to their GP, seek help, ask for help.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "If I knew I could seek help I would not have waited until I was expecting... because I did suffer a lot before." If you have been affected by the contents of the article, support is available through the BBC Action Line website .
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The largest teaching union had objected to the prospect of partly funding a 3.5% pay increase this year out of existing school budgets Schools in England are to get around £500 million in extra funding towards the teachers' pay award this school year, reducing the risk of a strike ballot by the largest education union.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Schools had been expected to fund some of the 3.5% teachers pay increase for the current school year out of their existing budgets, which National Education Union (NEU) leaders had strongly objected to.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Daniel Kebede, the general secretary of the NEU, said the offer of more funding was a "significant" step in negotiations.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: In a letter to the union on Wednesday, which has been seen by the BBC, the government said the increase would be funded by savings in employers' contributions to the local government pension scheme.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The letter said the 4.9 percentage point drop in what employers are expected to contribute will deliver "significant savings" on the pay bill for support staff, which will not be clawed back by central government.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The National Education Union said it expected the extra money to be around £500m, which schools can now use towards teachers' pay this year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: In July, ministers accepted the recommendation of the independent pay review body for teachers and agreed a 3.5% increase from September 2026 would be followed by 3% the following year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The pay increase had been partly funded by an additional £700m for 2026-27 and £1.1bn for the following year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Independent economists at the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) said that left schools facing a shortfall of around 1% between rising costs and funding this year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Luke Sibieta, IFS research fellow, said the extra money would mean the pay increase this year was fully funded - and on top of other funding increases, schools would be £1.6bn better off by next year than they had expected this summer.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The additional money could potentially bring the uplift for this year into line with next year.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Kebede said schools has been "running on empty" and the funding signalled "a welcome return to reality, and a message of hope for the entire school community".
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of the National Association of Headteachers, said the decision is "certainly welcome", putting schools in a "better position".
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: He said his union would look carefully at the detail "to determine whether this means the pay uplift is genuinely fully funded" for schools.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said he was "pleased" at the announcement of additional funding but "the wider pressure on school and college budgets remains intense".
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Similarly, the NASUWT union welcomed the news.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: General secretary Matt Wrack added schools needed "a sustainable, long-term injection of extra funding" to meet the needs of young people.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: In an indicative ballot by the NEU in April, 90% of teachers who voted said they would be prepared to take industrial action over funding and pay, on a turnout of 48%.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: A formal ballot was due to begin on 3 October and close 15 December, raising the prospects of teachers pay strikes early in 2027.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: The national executive of the NEU will meet on 24 September to consider whether to call that off following the additional funding on offer from the government.
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: A spokesperson for Education Secretary Lucy Powell said the government was "confident schools can now meet the costs of the award at a national level".
sentences.article_title: Schools in England get extra £500m in bid to avoid teachers' pay strike

sentences.text: Liberal Democrat schools spokesperson Caroline Voaden said she was "glad the government has seen sense, but schools shouldn't have gone through the stress of working out where the money would come from".

sentences.text: There will be a boost for fresh fruit and vegetables and deep-fried food will be banned in what the government has called the biggest shake-up to school dinners in England in over a decade.

sentences.text: Under new school food standards, fibre and wholegrains will also be increased, and breakfast clubs will have to follow nutrition rules for the first time, with schools also being monitored.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: The Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) welcomed the changes, but said they hoped the new rules would not become "another stick with which to beat head teachers".
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: The changes will come into effect from 2027 and be funded with existing money for schools, the government said.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: As part of the new framework, sweet desserts, like cake, will be reduced from a regular lunch offer to twice a week in secondary schools, and once a week in primary schools.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: They also must now be served with a portion of fruit.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: Servings of processed meats such as ham, sausages and chicken nuggets have been reduced to once a week and must come with a side of vegetables or fruit.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell said they were "once-in-a-generation changes" which would "transform school food for children across the country".
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: The Department for Education said it hoped the reforms would tackle childhood obesity, improve nutrition and support children's concentration, learning and wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: Schools will be required to publish food policies and menus online with monitoring arrangements set to be developed alongside the Food Standards Agency, it said.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, ASCL general secretary, said parents would feel "reassured" that schools were providing children with a healthy diet.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: But on plans for enforcement, he added: "None of us would consider ourselves experts in health and nutrition.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: Schools Minister Georgia Gould told BBC Breakfast she was confident schools could deliver healthy meals within existing budgets, without diverting funding from elsewhere, like teaching, and that schools would be given a year to implement the changes.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: She said the government was "absolutely determined to support schools" to redesign their menus affordably.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: As part of the changes, deep-fried chips will have to be oven-baked instead, and pasta dishes will need to be 50% wholewheat once a week.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: High-fibre bread will also become a requirement.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: Under the new rules, all dishes must come with at least one portion of fruit or vegetables Breakfast clubs will undergo one of the biggest changes.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: Historically, there has been no guidance on what they should provide, but from next September pastries and fried-eggs will be off the menu and there will be a sugar cap when it comes to cereals.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: The government said Coco Pops would no longer be an option and chocolate spread was "not permitted".
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: Since February this year, 1,250 schools have offered free breakfast clubs to their pupils.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: One of those was Oasis Academy Blakenhale in Birmingham, where principal Farzana Ahmed said the school welcomed the changes.
sentences.article_title: Deep-fried food banned under new school dinner rules in England

sentences.text: "The more children that can access a hot, nutritious meal, the better it is for us, the better it is for them, and actually it really supports families with the reduction of their financial pressures at home," she said.

sentences.text: Ahmed said it was "important" that schools are monitored, but added that they "probably need some more guidance from the government on what that's going to look like on a day-to-day basis".

sentences.text: "It's a really positive move," she said.

sentences.text: There could be tens of thousands more teenagers who are not in education, employment or training (Neet) than official statistics suggest, the children's commissioner for England has warned.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: A report by Dame Rachel de Souza said around 42,000 16- and 17-year-olds in England were officially classed as studying at college, but were not showing up at least half of the time.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: She said they had gone "under the radar" and were "not getting the support that they need".
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: The Department for Education (DfE) said it planned to help colleges track attendance and ultimately to gather that data centrally.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Unlike schools, further education and sixth form colleges in England are not required to collect or report attendance data.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Dame Rachel's report is based on attendance data obtained from 262 college groups in England and says rates are "substantially lower" than in schools.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: It suggests that more than half (52.2%) of 16- and 17-year-olds are estimated to be persistently absent by the standards used in schools, meaning they are missing 10% or more of college sessions.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: And around 42,000 (5.9%) are severely absent, meaning they are missing at least half of college sessions.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: The DfE estimates that 57,000 16- and 17-year-olds in England are Neet, and Dame Rachel's report argues that these persistently absent teenagers should be considered as "hidden" Neets alongside them.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Dame Rachel told the BBC a range of factors led to teenagers missing college, including part-time work and travel costs, and that some had been largely absent from education since the Covid pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: She said while those juggling part-time employment were likely to miss college every so often, it was those who are "far more vulnerable" who were likely to be severely absent.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: She added that it was "shocking" that the DfE did not collect the data as it meant the issue was "ignored".
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: "It's under the radar and these kids are not getting the support that they need," she said.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: "Sometimes the student being able to be offered that £30 shift there and then means more... than the potential qualification in six or seven months' time," he said.

sentences.text: University applicants in England will be given clearer information about student loans before they take them out, the government has said.

sentences.text: Ministers said they would spell out that governments can change repayment rules and that different career choices can affect how much borrowers repay.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The recent debate has centred around Plan 2 loans, which were issued in England between September 2012 and July 2023, and are still issued in Wales.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The interest rate on those loans is the Retail Prices Index (RPI) measure of inflation plus up to 3% depending on earnings, and borrowers repay at a rate of 9% of everything they earn over a repayment threshold, which is meant to rise with inflation every year.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The loans are written off after 30 years.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Campaigners want a lower interest rate, a lower repayment rate and for the government to reverse a decision last year to freeze the threshold at £29,385 for three years in England.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Freezing that threshold means graduates start repaying their loans sooner and, once they do, they pay more than they would have done if it had risen with inflation.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: MPs on the Treasury Committee called for a U-turn on that decision as part of a series of recommendations after an inquiry this summer.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.

sentences.text: Experts recommend that those who may be more vulnerable - such as older people and babies and young children - should take extra precautions.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: As the body gets hotter, blood vessels open up.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This lowers your blood pressure and makes your heart work harder to push the blood around the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This process can cause mild symptoms such as an itchy heat rash or swollen feet.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: At the same time, sweating leads to the loss of fluids and salt and, crucially, the balance between them in the body changes.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This, combined with the lowered blood pressure, can lead to heat exhaustion.

sentences.text: A common symptom of the menopause is a hot flush Partners of women going through the menopause are being invited to experience one of the symptoms at a forthcoming support event.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: At the Menopaus'ull Support Network event in Hull next month, health group Over The Bloody Moon will be taking one of its MenoVests, allowing people to experience a hot flush – one of the symptoms of the menopause.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Sarah Weichardt, who co-manages the project, said: "We're particularly interested in getting men along to come and experience the MenoVest, just so that they can understand what women go through." The event will be at Princes Quay shopping centre on 17 October, from 10:30 until 14:30 BST.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: "It's not just a hot flush, it's what the hot flush brings with it," said Weichardt.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: "So it could be panic, it could be anxiety.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: It's experiencing it all at the same time." She said she hoped the vest would give people a "better understanding of what women are going through".
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: "The more people we can get to experience it, the better," she added.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: The menopause describes the end of a woman's reproductive years, and often happens at about the age of 50.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: The period leading up to this is called the perimenopause, which is when many women notice their periods becoming unpredictable.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Other symptoms can include mood shifts, difficulty sleeping, and discomfort during sex.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Weichardt said her organisation had a banner with nearly 40 symptoms on it.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Many women "don't necessarily know that they're going into the menopause or they're perimenopausal" until they see the banner – and then they sometimes have a "lightbulb moment", she said.
sentences.article_title: Invitation for men to 'experience hot flushes'

sentences.text: Once women have "accepted it and are happy" they are menopausal or peri-menopausal, they can seek the support they need, she added.

sentences.text: El Niño set to be 'strongest in living memory', says Met Office What is El Niño and why could it mean record temperatures?

sentences.text: El Niño is a naturally-occurring pattern, which happens about every two to seven years and tends to last for around a year.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Trade winds that typically blow from east to west across the Pacific Ocean can weaken or even reverse, allowing warm water to spread eastwards.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Heat is then released from the ocean into the atmosphere which can boost global temperatures and drive changes in weather patterns around the world.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Forecasters track the development of El Niño by watching temperatures in a key region of the Pacific Ocean.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: When these are consistently 0.5C above normal, an El Niño is declared.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: There are different ways of measuring the strength of El Niño, however.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: The records that have now been broken relate to daily measurements of sea surface temperature compared with the long term historical average.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: This is called the Oceanic Niño Index (ONI).
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Many scientists - including forecasters in the USA and Australia - also consider an alternative measure known as the Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI).
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: This measures how warm the key El Niño region is relative to the rest of the tropical oceans, meaning it takes into account the background warming caused by climate change.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: By the RONI index the current El Niño is not yet a record-breaker - but it is likely that more announcements will follow in the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Professor Adam Scaife, Head of Long Range Prediction at the Met Office, said: "We have been signalling for months that the developing El Niño will be an unprecedented event.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: "The fact that it has already exceeded previous records – with several weeks to go before it peaks later this year – shows the enormity of this El Niño." Every El Niño is different, therefore impacts on global weather patterns are not guaranteed.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: And the unprecedented strength of this El Niño does not necessarily mean it will have unprecedented impacts on the weather.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: September's full Moon will be visible in UK skies this weekend, just days after the autumn equinox.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: Known as the Harvest Moon, it will reach its fullest point at 17:49 BST on Saturday 26 September.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: At that time it will still be below the horizon for much of the UK, but it will rise shortly afterwards and appear almost completely full throughout Saturday evening.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: It gets its name from being the full Moon closest to the autumn equinox, which this year took place on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: September's full Moon is traditionally associated with the harvest, because historically, the additional moonlight after sunset was useful to farmers gathering crops.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: The Royal Observatory Greenwich also lists the Corn Moon as another common name, reflecting the crops traditionally harvested around this time of year.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: However, it does not always fall in September and if October's full Moon is closer to the autumn equinox, it takes the title instead.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: Five night sky events to look out for this autumn Your pictures as equinox marks the start of astronomical autumn The 2025 Harvest Moon, seen here rising over the City of London, was on 7 October If you catch the Moon as it rises it may appear yellow, orange or even reddish.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: This is not a special feature of the Harvest Moon, but simply that when it lies low in the sky and is close to the horizon, its light has to travel through more of the Earth's atmosphere before reaching our eyes.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: More of the shorter blue wavelengths of light are scattered, allowing the yellows, oranges and reds to become more prominent.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: However, there is some cloud further west and rain for parts of Scotland and Northern Ireland by the evening.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: The best chance of clearer skies currently looks to be across some southern and eastern parts of the UK, while conditions are expected to be more changeable elsewhere.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: The exact times of the moonrise will vary across the UK but will be shortly after it  reaches its fullest point.
sentences.article_title: When and how to see the Harvest Moon in 2026

sentences.text: The FBI is investigating a claim by a cyber-crime group that it has stolen sensitive information on all bureau staff - around 38,000 people.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: The group, Shiny Hunters, says it has every agent's name, role, badge number and personal details including home address, phone numbers and spouse information.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: Professor Ciaran Martin, the former head of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre, said - if confirmed - it was "as serious as it gets when it comes to data breaches." In a statement posted on X, the FBI said it was aware of the claim and the agency was  "actively and aggressively investigating the matter".
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: The criminals claim to have breached the FBI's servers on Monday night and began contacting reporters on Tuesday sharing samples and screenshots of the stolen data.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: The BBC has seen a small portion of the data, which appears to be genuine.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: According to Reuters, some of the data contains details about officials' ​job assignments, including sensitive work against Chinese spies, Russian intelligence and drug cartels.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: ShinyHunters is an international collective of hackers, believed to have originally started in France.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: It has been behind a number of high-profile breaches including on Rockstar Games in April and a highly disruptive hack on education platform Canvas in May.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: The group claims to have found a vulnerability in the Oracle cloud storage system used by the FBI to breach multiple systems including FBIJOBS, FBI BEAST, which does background checks on employees and applicants, FBI MedLink, which holds agent's medical records and FBI BICS, which holds investigation information.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: In its message on the dark web, the group said it did not hack the FBI system for money.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: Instead, the cyber-criminals are asking the agency to retract an advisory that it issued in May about the gang, saying it was "offended" by its characterisation.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: That FBI's public service announcement , external described ShinyHunters as "threat actors" who often "use their real or exaggerated claims of access to sensitive or personal information to prompt payment from victims".
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: "They target major companies across tech, finance, and retail, often stealing millions of customer records at once," the advisory said.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: ShinyHunters said it would give the bureau one week to correct or remove what it says are false allegations or they would publish the full databases.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: The FBI did not respond to multiple requests for comment from the BBC.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: In its statement on X, the agency said it was trying to determine whether or not the hackers had breached its systems or a third party.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: "We are actively and aggressively investigating this matter and working closely with those third-party providers that support FBIJobs.gov to mitigate any and all risk," the post said.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: In a statement to the BBC, a cyber-security expert said it was a "retaliation attack", which demonstrated that "no organisation is safe from the group".
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: "The group clearly wants to control the narrative around their activities, ensuring nothing is said that could dent their reputation," said William Wright of Closed Door Security.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: Meanwhile Andrew Brandt of cyber-security firm Huntress said it may provoke the FBI to track down and prosecute members of the hacking group.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents

sentences.text: "ShinyHunters must feel pretty confident they won't get caught to threaten a government agency like this," he said.
sentences.article_title: FBI investigating claim hackers have stolen details of all its agents
